 Bihar CM Samrat Chaudhary distributes ration cards, pledges no one sleeps hungry 
 By
 TNM (With ANI Inputs) 
 ✓
 12 November 2026, 2:32 pm 
 4 min read
 12 Nov 2026 
 ANI Photo | Bihar CM Samrat Chaudhary distributes ration cards, pledges no one sleeps hungry 
 Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Chaudhary distributed ration cards to below poverty line (BPL) families and issued new public distribution system (PDS) licences to shopkeepers at Gyan Bhawan in Patna on November 12. Addressing the recipients, he expressed his commitment to realising the visions of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and former Bihar Chief Minister Nitish Kumar for a developed India and prosperous Bihar.
 “I congratulate and thank everyone. My goal is much bigger. I will be happy when Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s dream of a developed India and Nitish Kumar’s vision of a prosperous Bihar are fulfilled,” Chaudhary said in a press release.

 The Chief Minister urged all present to take a pledge that “no poor person in Bihar should ever sleep hungry. Every poor person should have a ration card.” He stated that 20.9 million ration cards have already been issued across Bihar, emphasising that a ration card ensures food security for recipients.
 Chaudhary noted that although 2.4 million people are currently covered under the scheme, many families remain without ration cards and should apply. “Your ration card will be issued within 30 days, and you will receive all the benefits through it,” he assured.
 ADVERTISEMENT 
 Highlighting other government achievements, the Chief Minister mentioned the enrolment of millions in the Ayushman Bharat health insurance scheme. “We made a policy in 2024 to connect everyone with Ayushman Bharat cards so that they could receive healthcare benefits. The Central Government initially gave approval for around 65 million people, and another 27.5 million were added,” he said.
 On the government’s election success, Chaudhary explained, “We provide 125 units of free electricity to 19.2 million people in villages. People ask how Modi Ji and Nitish Ji keep winning elections. This is the formula. Some people come up with new formulas and consider themselves very smart. But the public is the real master. It decides whom to bring onto the stage and whom to remove from it.”
 Chaudhary also urged support for Panchayat Development Day, observed on the final Sunday of each month in Bihar. “Our target is one crore people, but we have achieved only one-fourth of it so far. We need to organise camps and run this campaign actively. I also request the District Magistrates to contribute and help us achieve this target,” he said.
 ADVERTISEMENT 
 He further spoke about Seva Sankalp and Kayakalp Diwas campaigns aimed at village improvements. “Before March 31, we have to improve the villages of Bihar. Kayakalp means improving the entire village. Schools and Anganwadi centres must be improved. Community buildings and Chhath ghats should also be constructed,” Chaudhary added.
 Addressing the issue of migrant labourers leaving Bihar, the Chief Minister acknowledged the importance of welfare, employment and government jobs over the next five years. “We have to focus on welfare work, employment and government jobs. We aim to provide government jobs and employment opportunities to one crore people. We need to develop the industrial sector. Around 450,000 people go outside Bihar for labour work. By 2030, we want to build a strong economy where people can work in good industries, but they should not have to leave Bihar for labour work,” he said.
 On food security, Chaudhary said, “Under the National Food Security Act, we have to ensure that ration reaches every household. We will achieve a food procurement target of 5 million metric tonnes. At present, Bihar has achieved procurement of around 3.4 to 3.5 million metric tonnes. We have to increase it further.”
 The Chief Minister also announced measures to assist elderly residents, stating, “My government will make sure that people, in the same way like those above 80 years of age who wanted to sell their land, could get the registration process completed at their homes; we will have people above 75 years of age receive rations at their homes. Earlier, this facility was available only to people above 80 years of age. This will be implemented from next year.”
 In conclusion, Chaudhary expressed gratitude to both leaders. “I thank Prime Minister Narendra Modi for providing free food grains. This scheme started during the COVID-19 pandemic. I also thank Nitish Ji for implementing this system. Both are great leaders,” he said.
